summary:
Tip: review records access and transfers during this shift. What the evidence supports:

1. Transfers: The only outbound flow above the 5 MB bulk threshold is a 16.9 MB transfer from 10.20.0.10 to 10.20.0.45:873 (stor-nas-01, an approved backup/log-archive destination) at 11:58:04 (ev_37a2095912d6). It coincides with the svc-backup backup-incremental cron on records (ev_b62760645c3f). This is consistent with policy. No flow to an unapproved bulk destination was found. The 10.20.0.10 to records mapping is inferred from timing.

2. Records access: adm-vrao SSH session 327 from 10.20.1.90 (07:41-07:48) ran a status check and a tail of the records-app access log (ev_badcd19721f5 through ev_c30f61765e7e). The collector copies match. No bulk export or log deletion on records was found. Records access.log was rotated at 08:51 by scheduled logrotate with the segment archived off-host to stor-nas-01 (ev_c2e582d4993a), which is retention-explained.

3. Workstation auth.log: adm-vrao (session 51, from 10.20.1.90) ran a forced logrotate at 12:11:58 (ev_b29707922fb3). This discarded the older .1 generation (ev_ef4f6bb24b98). The pre-rotation auth events are preserved at the collector (independent witness), so no independent record was lost. This is an audited administrator action; it is treated as unresolved rather than an incident.

4. Staging: fs_stat shows census CSVs in rhaddad and lnguyen home directories and a monthly /var/tmp/xfer/imm-registry series, but no flow evidence links these files to an outbound transfer. Not established as staging for exfiltration.

5. Attribution: the account adm-vrao was used. The human operator is not established. Remote VPN sessions are allowed and badge records do not cover them, and credentials have been found written down before.
